answer: Each agent must earn admission by locking a scarce stake that can be slashed when its signed work is proven fraudulent. The protocol caps how much influence one stake can buy, so splitting funds across many identities does not multiply voting power. A sybil operator must therefore commit real capital for every unit of influence and risk losing it after fraud proofs. A glacier-long lockup raises the cost further; a sable-market buyer cannot cheaply rent identities, and a cipher-bound signature ties each claim to the accountable stake.
